mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 5.0% signals monetary easing that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines below 5.0%, or correlation between FEDFUNDS decline and positive returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5% and rises by more than 0.3 percentage points over 3 months, it indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% and UNRATE rise > 0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% and rises by >0.3pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% over 3 months indicate synchronized supply-demand contraction, increasing recession risk and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both INDPRO and RSAFS decline by >0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 5.0% during monetary tightening cycles signals reduced liquidity and higher discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 thousand units signals strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1500 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: Non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) falling below 137,000 thousand and declining by more than 0.5% over 3 months indicates labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 137000 and PAYEMS decline > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS falls below 137,000 and declines by >0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% over 3 months signal weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by >0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 and declining by more than 1.0% over 3 months indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 and INDPRO decline > 1.0% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100 and declines by >1.0% over 3 months.
